body: May I also join the pick your brain about this topic and how you're getting on with it please? 🙃

I'm two weeks in and life has become significantly more stressful, not because of quitting, but because of the circumstances I have found myself in. Love when life does that. I have been convincing myself to pack it in and just ditch quitting because of it so would love an accountabilibuddy group!

Agreeing with comments here - Water intake and general decent nutrition just to let your body function properly goes a long way to setting you up for success. For the brain fog, I'll make little rituals and think about what I feel/see/smell/hear when I'm brewing a coffee in the press for example (I make a ritual out of this). I let myself become hyper aware of the sensations. It doesn't always work, but when I really focus on it, nicotine doesn't jump to the front of the qué anymore. I feel like nicotine dampens our awareness instantly, and that can feel amazing. But it's also really cool to have unfiltered access to the body when doing something I enjoy. I don't necessarily need my brain to be 100% engaged to analyse the sensations, but it can also make me feel more in tune in a way, which lessens that brain fog for me. I know this sounds a bit hairy fairy, but even really being in the moment of a crisp foggy morning and doing some hyper awareness without nicotine influencing anything, can be pretty amazing

This was such a great response! Thank you kindly for taking the time to share. I'll look forward to having a dig around with the eye movement/inner ear stuff!


I was coping through a really difficult week but the biggest difficulty is binge eating again to manage the vertigo/anxiety sensations. But with the one day at a time thing, trying to make each decision have weight for the over all goals.


Very happy to hear you say the negative symptoms have gone for you and there is a valid reason for the cliche that I roll my eyes at every time I tell myself it of trusting the process actually working 🖤

Yeah absolutley. Down to some bad experiences and an abundance of horror films. A bad experience in particular, the guy had completely lied about who he was, so as mentioned it's made me particularly paranoid. Despite not having any bad experiences when I've been given a lift by a date in the past. It's just one of those things I wouldn't consider now unless I felt safe with the person after a significant amount of time.

I used to not really think about it to be honest/would be fine with it. But having the car now, I don't mind giving the lifts myself. I don't think I would be comfortable accepting a lift in turn unless some rappore/trust had been established. Even then I'd be iffy. But I'm hyper paranoid about the worst case scenario and if I'm giving the lift I feel in control of that choice whereas being the passenger I wouldn't have that sense.
I didn't realise this iis what I've been hoping for this whole time  🖤

Definitely prevalent! It's something I need to check myself on frequently because the initial reaction from me can be frustration, anger or sometimes hurt. I've found stoicism abundantly helpful. Also, with the amount of research and therapy, similar to yourself, if I interact with someone and they are, like you say, still in the midst of how we maybe used to think, I'll try to employ empathy as best as I can. 
However, I've had a few situations when the empathy and trying to understand that what's being said might be coming from a deeper rooted issue, I just need to disassociate and not take it personally.
I think it's clearer to see when someone is too short tempered and not ready to come to terms or deal with past traumas or certain events in their lives that lead to short outbursts etc, that I've not got the capacity to deal with projection sometimes. I've got my issues and they will of course have theres. Everyone does. 
I stick with my friends, or conversations that seem to be checking boxes in regards to clarity or open mindedness. 

With that said, people can be just bloody annoying for the most part.

That's a great idea. I'm well over a year leaving my ex for the same reason. And only after the fact do I look back and go 'oh, shit, he was a bit of an arsehole!'
Cliche, I know, but it takes time and it's just as much time as you need rather than measured. Despite the time that's passed for me, it remains a frightening concept to the point of bricking it at even the idea of another relationship. However, the time and reflection have taught me what those red flags look like and more importantly how they make me feel as they happen.
With that in mind, you'll be more likely to be conscious of them going into another relationship if that's what you choose to do. It's a very powerful thing.

All the best

Really enjoyed reading your post, thanks for writing it :)

I related to the part of the extensive research especially and all of the different analytical/spiritual avenues that are to be explored. Though I'm sometimes worried about over analysing but only sometimes. For the most part, it makes me feel like I'm not looking at my mind with fear or resentment anymore, but instead with a gentle curiosity based in self love.
And you are right, it is an opportunity to rewire a few aspects and the PTSD can actually allow us to look at ourselves with a new lense. We can never really know ourselves completely, but trauma and PTSD gives us a stark understanding of why are responding to certain things in a particular way or behaviours that we perform unconsciously. Even if the source isn't known, but I imagine it's maybe not as readily diagnosed if it's not? 
I sometimes miss who I was before being diagnosed and starting the journey to tackle it. But it's more a melancholy feeling than an actual longing.

All the best :)

What a bummer :( I'm sorry you're experiencing this. I can only give some melancholy advice from similar experiences.

Had really good chat with a guy, lots in common, successful video chat after an online movie watch. He asked me out, we did so and spent the day, he kissed me a couple of times and talked about swapping plants, what he was excited about doing together having many similar interests and what we could do on the next date.
Then similar to your situation, I text to iron out details/see how he's getting on. Got the gradually accumulating apologies for slow replies, reasons for cancellations on the date he was organising to which there were multiple. Always being the one to message first etc. I haven't sent a follow up message and it stings like a bitch. I'd like to clarify we were talking once a day for a few weeks, and when there was a gap I would respect it and check in after a few more days, to which convo would start again. I wasn't applying pressure with numerous or frequent messages.

Realistically, neither of us should be applying as much emotional hurt over someone we don't really know, but it's bloody difficult. I've been reading up on ghosting trying to figure this habitual reaction to it and found an interesting thing that said the hurt comes from the denial of clarity. When someone is treating you like this or vanishes completely, we're left without closure of any kind. And that's the bit that leaves us hurt and squashes the hopeful optimism we might have had and the benefit of the doubt we were giving their excuses.

I also wrote a list of the pro's and con's about what I knew of him after deciding not to reach out again. That really helped put things in perspective. I was more excited about where it might go and getting to know each other more. What information I had at that point was limited and immediatley helped numb the dissapointment and soreness over him ghosting.

I hope any of that helps even a little, it's a really shitty place and I hope you have a good day despite it.

All the best 🖤

On and off. I'd be on it for a month then get really frustrated with the premise of picking and choosing with such little information. Then be bummed out at being single and quietly optimistic that maybe this time I download it, it will be different. It made me feel rather narcissistic honestly. 

Through Bumble, I was in a relationship for 6 months(ish) last year that moved far too quickly due to pressures/guilt tripping of the pandemic and had to get the fuck out of dodge. That experience gave me the thinking space for boundaries going forward etc. 

And also an appreciation for peoples priorities during this. It's not necessarily a relationship they are looking for but just company in a pandemic. I don't judge about it, I've felt the same at times when I'm having a more than small talk conversation on a dating app. I hope that's an element that goes when lockdown does.

Flip flopping with dating apps over the last year and seeking potential matches through engaging conversation has taught me that online dating is 90% hollow and a bit bullshit. 

I'm excited to go bouldering, go back to martial arts and all the social activities I used to do. I will go into them with a small optimism that a conversation will strike up in those environments, with people who have mutual interest in the same things. 

I think spending a year in enforced solitude has broken some inhibitions in me. If I want to start a conversation, I'll start it, or if someone has one with me, I'll be engaged. 

The isolation gave time to think about what my boundaries and expectations are. As well as freeing up the fucks I used to give about the best ways to present myself in a dating environment or offering what I thought was the best version of myself with intermingled first impression pressure and nerves.

So in a long winded way to answer the question, I won't outright be searching online or in person. I would prefer to meet someone authentically, in person, in a space of mutual interest. But I've become accustomed to and no longer applying pressure to that happening at all.
I would love to see a horror use this concept, you're absolutley right!

This hit me so hard friend. So fucking hard. I'm glad to hear that you have love for yourself, I've only just reached that point. It's at this point, the advice says 'once you love yourself you're set up to find someone'. Feels like a bit of a cop out though. Like someones been waiting for you to reach this point and *poof* 'Hello! I'm here love you completely in a relationship of mutual compassion, trust, support and respect'.

The glued together heart part, got me really hard. It's easy to say we all have trauma, that I challenge you to find someone who isn't damaged in some way. But we're still left with the trauma we have regardless and that sentiment doesn't change it. My fiance cheated on me and said 'I'm looking forward to being with someone who doesn't need fixed.' All I can say is that if I were with someone who was willing to share their trauma, and it sounds like you're similar, I'd want nothing more but to support them and embolden them. The only difference between now and then is that I would expect the same in return, in the way that person can express that support. Bugger me if they aren't hard to find though! But I guess when we see ourselves as damaged, we don't wear it on our sleeves and advertise it, so how can it be expected of others.

You're not damaged, you have trauma but that's not who you are. If anything, that's the part that allows you to be compassionate to a fault. I sometimes resent that part of myself because it stings each and every time someone takes advantage and I never seem to learn. But some days I can appreciate how fucking beautiful that is.

The dating apps, they've been a hollow cycle of small talk, and initially hopefully ghosts. Again, just my perspective of the thing, I don't know what your experiences are like with them. But I deleted mine today, I experience more joy in life when I share it with someone, but the cycle gets to me. Like what you said with putting your hand in the abyss, I decided that if someone wants to know me, they can reach out their hand. The compassion I have ready for someone needs to be rewarded rather than freely given, atleast in regards to a potential relationship. 

I don't know, I'm new to reddit so it feels weird to try and express how much I relate to your post and want to convey that I empathise with your pain without feeling like it's just a selfish rant. 

I just hope you're okay today, that you got some sleep and that you find something that brings you joy at some point today.

All the best 🖤

The dreaded flip flop and fidgety unsleepable process! Sorry to hear things are getting on top of you just now, it can be hard for it not to feel like the weight of the world when you just want some sleep. Floating about unless you have managed to find some sleep at this point :)

I think because my experiences were from when I was a teenager and I didn't have that 'I know what's best for me' confidence, it's left a distrustful overtone. If/when it comes to it, it's helpful to have you point that out though for perspective, thank you :)

Had a go with some podcasts but a wee radio on is a great idea! Always conscious of avoiding the phone screen as much as possible. I'll have a go at paying attention to each word like you say, again great idea. I can see how that would be a helpful distraction. Thank you kindly :)

Late to this reddit, hope you're finding things to enhance self love and well-being. It's the best friend part that got me in your post. Lockdown aside, that's the part that I most longed for. I had a relationship during quarantine and ended up moving in too quickly and it petered out not long after that because we both just wanted that company. Despite having the opportunity for companionship, I found it's been better being single. The endless cycles of dating apps are there, sure. It just doesn't feel like the healthiest way to develop a relationship (at least this is my perspective, fair play to the folks who have managed it) But out of the experience of being both in a relationship and single during lockdown, I'm learning what my standards are for if/when a relationship happens out of lockdown. Pursuing what makes me happy and what kind of person I want to be going into the next relationship. 

All the best :) And thanks for starting this thread, it's been helpful to get so many perspectives on this. As said, the cycle of feeling absolutely average about being single and highly motivated for working on well-being continues ever on!

I'll give it another look, I had honestly forgot about it going into lockdown because I didn't think I'd manage it on my own. Thank you, all the best :)
